quotes.text: This is the true beginning of the Balaam story. The repetition of the subject and the use of synonymous verbs and objects, a characteristic of Hebrew poetry, may actually be due to a poetic substratum underlying the text. See-the next verse.

If I had a sword "[The Moabite officials] said: This fool [boasts] that he can destroy nations with his words; how can he not destroy his ass except with a sword?" The irony rests in the fact that the sword Balaam seeks is close at hand with the angel, whom he, the seer, cannot see.

Her gentle spirit then saluted me and withdrew. I came to
myself. The doleful noise of the guards, and the wrangling and
angry words of the old apostate again grated on my ears, but Heaven
and hope were in my soul.
